findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic
findings.body: This read-modify-write can let concurrent login requests both validate the same backup code. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other’s updates because each writes a stale copy of the entire encrypted list, restoring a code that was already consumed. This breaks the promised one-time-use guarantee and allows backup-code replay; consume codes with an atomic compare-and-swap or equivalent serialized update.

findings.title: The setup password visibility toggle cannot reveal the password
findings.body: This field passes `type="password"` to `PasswordField`. That component sets its visibility-dependent type before spreading the supplied props, so this fixed type overrides the component’s `text` type when the eye toggle is clicked. Remove the explicit type or change the component so the toggle can reveal the password.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is no longer keyboard reachable
findings.body: Setting `tabIndex={-1}` removes the show/hide password button from the Tab order for every `PasswordField`. Keyboard-only users can no longer focus or activate this control; keep it keyboard reachable.

findings.title: The new backup-code login flow is not covered by an end-to-end test
findings.body: The added test exercises displaying, downloading, and copying codes, but never attempts login with a backup code or verifies that a consumed code is rejected. The central authentication behavior—and its one-time-use contract—can therefore regress while this test still passes; add coverage for successful backup-code login and reuse rejection.
